UCI World Championships Women’s Individual Time-Trial 2026: Our form guide

The women’s elite time-trial at the UCI World Championships takes place on Sunday 20th September in Montreal, Canada. On the same 39.2km course with 220m elevation as the men, the riders will depart from Avenue du Parc and head over the Saint Lawrence River before taking in Circuit Gilles Villeneuve, where another bridge crossing sees them return towards the Parc Jeanne Mance via a few twists and turns past the Rue Notre-Dame.

Last year in Rwanda, Marlen Reusser (Switzerland) finally won the time-trial gold medal that had somehow previously eluded her. The Netherlands duo of Anna van der Breggen and Demi Vollering completed the podium.

Marlen Reusser (Switzerland)

Switzerland’s Marlen Reusser is looking strong in her defence of the time-trial title. Utterly dominating against the clock this season, the 34-year-old has won ITT stages at the Tour de Suisse and the Tour de France Femmes, only failing to win on the Giro d’Italia TT to Anna van der Breggen, which was an uphill time-trial.

There have been four different winners of this title in the past four years, however Reusser should provide some stability if she does what she does best.

  • Best ITT result this season: 1st place x 3 (Tour de Suisse Women, Tour de France Femmes, Chrono Féminin de Gatineau)
  • Best World Championship ITT result: 1st (2025)

Zoe Bäckstedt (Great Britain)

Time-trials are Zoe Bäckstedt’s forte. Even though she is only 21 years old, the Brit possesses a palmarès most could only dream of in the discipline with national and European success. This year she’s chosen to step up to the elite field instead of defending her U23 crown where she’s aiming to dethrone Reusser – their last meeting came at the Tour de France Femmes where Bäckstedt raced to fourth.

This year, Bäckstedt has claimed victory in four time-trials including the prologue and ITT at the Baloise Ladies Tour where she defended her overall title. Her last TT against Reusser was at the Tour de France Femmes, where Bäckstedt finished fourth and Reusser won.

  • Best ITT result this season: 1st place x 4 (Vuelta a Extremadura, British National Championships, Baloise Ladies Tour)
  • Best World Championship ITT result: 1st (2025 U23, 2022 Junior)

Demi Vollering (Netherlands)

It’s been quite the year for the Netherlands’ Demi Vollering. After sweeping up a host of Classics victories in the spring, she won the Giro with a daring final day attack and then became the first rider to win multiple editions of the Tour de France Femmes. In terms of time-trials, she has been consistent this season, taking third in both the Giro and Tour TTs.

Vollering claimed Worlds ITT silver in 2024 and bronze in 2025, and any slip up from Reusser could open the door for a victory in Canada. She has won so much throughout her career, but a rainbow jersey is one thing she’s missing.

  • Best ITT result this season: 3rd place x 2 (Giro d’Italia, Tour de France Femmes)
  • Best World Championship ITT result: 2nd (2024)

Antonia Niedermaier (Germany)

Antonia Niedermaier has really shone this season with second overall at the Giro and fourth at the Tour. She narrowly missed out on her National Championships ITT defence, taking second place but she tends to perform well at the World Championships, finishing fourth in 2024 and sixth in 2025.

  • Best ITT result this season: 2nd place (German National Championships)
  • Best World Championship ITT result: 3rd (2023, Junior)

Lieke Nooijen (Netherlands)

Lieke Nooijen has really kicked things up a notch in 2026. The 25-year-old finished third in the ITT at the Dutch National Championships but won the road race before her star performance on Stage 4 of the Tour where she rocketed to second place in the ITT, beating the likes of Vollering and Bäckstedt.

She absolutely has a shot at a medal here, despite not having competed at this level in the time-trial before, her best international placing being fifth in the European Championships last year.

  • Best ITT result this season: 2nd place (Tour de France Femmes)
  • Best World Championship ITT result: N/A

Other contenders

There are plenty more riders who could ride their way to a medal on Sunday.

Norwegian ITT Champion Katrine Aalerud finished 2025 by racing to fifth in the World Championships and fourth in the European Championships ITT, while compatriot Mie Bjørndal Ottestad won a silver medal in the Europeans. Finnish ITT Champion Anniina Ahtosalo raced to second in the U23 ITT at the European Championships last year too.

Cédrine Kerbaol will carry French hopes alongside the in-form Juliette Berthet, while her EF teammate Kristen Faulkner will be flying the stars and stripes.

There are several big names in the TT who will be more focused on the road race but could ride to a medal including Belgium’s Lotte Kopecky, German National Champion Franzi Koch, Poland’s Dominika Włodarczyk and Spanish breakthrough star Paula Blasi.
